source_documents.title: On the Planarity of Heterocyclic Bay‐Substituted Perylenediimides: Insight into the Fluorescent Photoinduced Electron Transfer Sensing Framework

conditions_studied: solution (chloroform, THF, methanol, water; acid vs base)

reference_evidence_units.quote: the fluorescent pH indicators possess photoinduced electron transfer (PET) and internal charge transfer mechanisms with turn-on emission switching in the presence of acid.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PDIs 1-5
reference_evidence_units.statement: Acid turns emission on (PET from the dimethylaminoethyl receptors blocked); bay amines add ICT.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Counterintuitively, the dibrominated intermediate with two heavy atoms is more brightly emissive than the heterocyclic bay-substituted compounds.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 5 vs 1-4
reference_evidence_units.statement: The dibromo compound is the brightest.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Closer inspection of the heterocyclic compounds by density functional theory calculations reveals a non-planar bent or twisted geometry between the two naphthyl subunits.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Bay amines bend or twist the perylene core.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the pyrrolidine appears to have a bent geometry versus a twisted geometry for the fluorescent bromine derivative
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2 vs 5
reference_evidence_units.statement: Bent (pyrrolidine) vs twisted (bromo) core is linked to the brightness difference.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Bay amino donors give ICT; the paper names PET and ICT together as the sensing mechanisms.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Acid-activated turn-on via blocked PET from the dimethylaminoethyl receptors.
